concept.title: Troubleshooting
concept.shortdesc: Toolkit behaviours that publishers of large, key-based publications meet on DITA-OT 4.4, what they look like in the build log and on the page, and the remedy for each.

conbody.p: troubleshootingDITA-OTknown limitationsEverything below was characterised on a real publication of about ten thousand topics during the plugin's live trials. None of it is caused by the plugin, and none of it can be fixed by the plugin, because it happens in the toolkit's preprocessing before any rendering; a plain html5 build shows the same results. The plugin's part is to say so clearly.

section.title: Merged pages fail on DITA-OT 4.4: "Failed to move chunk"
section.p: chunkingDITA-OT 4.4DITA-OT 4.4 processes a DITA 1.x chunk="to-content" with its new DITA 2.0 chunking code in a compatibility mode. That code has three defects that a publication merging index pages from many topics is likely to meet:

ul.li: If the chunked submap is included both normally and as the target of a format="ditamap" key definition in a resource-only links map, the chunk is generated twice and the build reports Failed to move chunk. The merged page is missing, every link to it fails with DOTX031E, and links from the map to its sections warn with DOTX061W and DOTX026W.
copy-to on a chunked topicref is not honoured, so the merged page is written under the wrong name or not at all.
When the chunked topic is also the target of an ordinary key definition, the merge can be silently skipped: no message, and the page contains only its own topic.

section.p: The remedy is to switch the toolkit back to its earlier chunking code. In the toolkit installation, edit config/configuration.properties and change the line

to false. That file is the only place the setting is read; it cannot be passed on the command line, and installing or removing plugins leaves it untouched. Every toolkit you publish from needs the same edit, including any continuous-integration environment.

Alongside that, reference chunked submaps with <mapref href="..."> rather than by key, for the reason in the next section. Links from other topics to the merged page keep working: keys that name the chunked topic resolve to the merged page whatever its file name.

section.title: A section shows no link and no children: keys inside a keyref'd submap
section.p: keyskeyref'd maprefsGOVK001WDITA-OT 4.4.1 does not resolve any key inside a submap that was itself included with <mapref keyref="...">: a topicref or topicset whose target is a key gets no link, a nested <mapref keyref> is not included at all, and a keyed child topic is dropped from the tree. The same submap included with <mapref href="..."> resolves completely. On the page this appears as a sidebar or home-page entry rendered as plain text with nothing beneath it.
The toolkit reports nothing. The plugin does: each affected entry produces a build warning naming the entry and the key.
section.codeblock: Warning: [GOVK001W]: Navigation entry 'Data Sets' has keyref='data_sets_overview' that was not resolved, so it is rendered without a link and without children. DITA-OT does not resolve keys inside a map that is itself included with <mapref keyref="...">. Include that submap with <mapref href="..."> instead, or check that the key is defined.
section.p: Change the map references to use href. Keys that name whole maps are then usually unused and can be dropped from the links map, which also removes the double inclusion described above.

section.title: Links to topics merged into another page
section.p: A key that names a topic which chunk="to-content" merges into another page cannot be resolved by the toolkit after the merge, and every reference to it reports DOTX031E. Key the merged parent instead, with a fragment for the child (parent.dita#child-id). The design records the full analysis against a real corpus.
